text: Writing clean code is like telling a clear story to another developer. It is not just for computers; it is for people who will read your work later. The most important rule is to make your code readable. Use meaningful naming conventions, so a variable like `userAge` tells you exactly what it contains instead of a confusing `x`. Avoid writing long, complicated blocks of logic. Instead, break your work into small, focused functions that do one thing well. This makes the code easier to test and debug. Ultimately, clean code saves time and effort, ensuring your project’s maintainability for years to come.
